criteria.name: Root Cause Correctness
criteria.definition: Measures whether the agent correctly identifies the actual underlying cause of the incident relative to the known ground-truth fault.

classes.rubric: The identified root cause is unrelated to or contradicts the ground-truth root cause.
The agent identifies a related symptom, component, or general problem area, but attributes the incident to the wrong underlying cause.
The agent identifies the correct general fault category or causal mechanism but misses important aspects of the actual root cause.
The agent identifies the correct root cause with only minor inaccuracies, ambiguity, or missing specificity.
The agent correctly identifies the underlying root cause and relevant affected component at the level supported by the available evidence.

criteria.name: Causal Reasoning Quality
criteria.definition: Measures whether the agent provides a technically plausible and coherent causal explanation connecting the identified root cause to the observed symptoms.
criteria.evaluation_note: A correct root-cause conclusion should not automatically receive a high causal-reasoning score. The reasoning itself must establish the causal relationship.

classes.rubric: No meaningful causal explanation is provided, or the proposed reasoning contradicts the supplied evidence.
The explanation mainly reports correlations or makes causal assertions without explaining how the proposed root cause produces the observed symptoms.
The agent provides a reasonable causal mechanism, but important steps in the causal chain are missing or insufficiently justified.
The agent provides a coherent and technically plausible causal chain connecting the proposed root cause to the important observed symptoms.
The agent provides a clear, technically sound, and well-supported causal chain explaining how the root cause produced the important observed symptoms.

criteria.name: Evidence Grounding
criteria.definition: Measures the extent to which the agent's diagnosis and supporting claims are grounded in the telemetry, observations, logs, metrics, traces, or other evidence available during the incident.
criteria.evaluation_note: Technical plausibility alone does not constitute evidence grounding. A claim must be supported by evidence actually available to the agent. Judge only claims inside AGENT_RESULT against GROUND_TRUTH and CHAOS_MANIFESTS; tool traces are not supplied.

classes.rubric: Key claims are fabricated, contradicted by the supplied evidence, or have no meaningful evidential support.
The agent references limited relevant evidence but relies substantially on unsupported assumptions.
Relevant evidence supports the general diagnosis, but some important claims or causal conclusions remain unsupported.
Most important claims and conclusions are explicitly supported by relevant evidence, with only minor unsupported assumptions.
The diagnosis and causal explanation are consistently supported by the supplied evidence, with no material fabricated, contradictory, or unsupported claims.

criteria.name: Localization Accuracy
criteria.definition: Measures how accurately and precisely the agent identifies the location of the originating fault within the system, such as the affected node, service, deployment, pod, or resource.
criteria.evaluation_note: The agent should not be penalized for failing to identify a more granular component when that level of specificity cannot reasonably be inferred from the available evidence.

classes.rubric: The agent localizes the fault to an unrelated or incorrect component.
The agent identifies only a broad or partially related subsystem but fails to identify the actual affected area.
The agent identifies the correct general component or system layer but does not sufficiently localize the originating fault.
The agent identifies the correct affected component with only minor ambiguity or missing specificity.
The agent correctly identifies the originating fault location at the level of specificity justified by the available evidence and ground truth.

criteria.name: Diagnostic Completeness
criteria.definition: Measures whether the RCA sufficiently explains the important symptoms and observations associated with the incident and connects them to the identified root cause.
criteria.evaluation_note: Completeness does not require the agent to discuss every available metric. The evaluation should focus on whether the important evidence necessary to explain the incident has been addressed.

classes.rubric: The RCA fails to explain the major observed symptoms or substantially contradicts the observations.
The RCA explains only a small portion of the incident and leaves most important observations unexplained.
The RCA explains the primary symptom or root cause but leaves important observations or relationships unexplained.
The RCA explains most important observations and their relationship to the root cause, with only minor gaps.
The RCA provides a coherent explanation covering the important observed symptoms and their relationship to the identified root cause, without material omissions or contradictions.

criteria.name: Remediation Correctness
criteria.definition: Measures whether the proposed remediation appropriately addresses the identified or ground-truth root cause and is expected to mitigate or resolve the incident.
criteria.evaluation_note: A remediation that only treats an observed symptom should not receive the highest classification when a feasible action addressing the underlying cause is available.

classes.rubric: The proposed remediation does not address the root cause, addresses an unrelated problem, or is likely to worsen the incident.
The remediation targets a related symptom or component but does not meaningfully address the underlying root cause.
The remediation addresses the root cause to some extent and may improve the incident, but does not fully resolve the underlying problem or misses an important action.
The remediation appropriately addresses the root cause and is likely to resolve or substantially mitigate the incident, with only minor shortcomings.
The remediation directly and appropriately addresses the root cause and represents a technically appropriate action for resolving or mitigating the incident.

criteria.name: Technical Feasibility
criteria.definition: Measures whether the proposed remediation can realistically be executed in the given Kubernetes/cloud-native environment using the available system capabilities and operational mechanisms.
criteria.evaluation_note: Evaluate feasibility independently from correctness. A remediation may be executable but still be the wrong action for the incident.

classes.rubric: The remediation cannot realistically be executed in the described environment or relies on nonexistent, invalid, or fundamentally incompatible mechanisms.
The general idea may be technically possible, but the proposed execution contains major technical problems or requires capabilities that are not available.
The remediation is technically possible but requires significant modification, additional steps, or unresolved prerequisites before it can be safely executed.
The remediation is technically executable with only minor adjustments, assumptions, or implementation details missing.
The remediation is technically valid and executable in the given environment using the available operational capabilities.

criteria.name: Risk and Safety
criteria.definition: Measures whether the remediation minimizes unnecessary operational risk, limits potential blast radius, and avoids actions that could introduce additional service disruption.
criteria.evaluation_note: Risk should be evaluated relative to the incident. A disruptive action is not automatically incorrect when the severity of the incident justifies it.

classes.rubric: The remediation introduces severe or unjustified operational risk, has an excessive blast radius, or could significantly worsen service availability or data integrity.
The remediation introduces substantial avoidable risk or disruption relative to the severity and scope of the incident.
The remediation has meaningful operational risk, but the risk may be justified by the incident or can be controlled with additional safeguards.
The remediation has limited and proportionate operational risk, with only minor safety concerns or missing safeguards.
The remediation minimizes unnecessary disruption, has an appropriately limited blast radius, and includes or inherently provides suitable operational safeguards.

criteria.name: Evidence Alignment
criteria.definition: Measures whether the selected remediation logically follows from the observed evidence and diagnosed root cause rather than relying on unsupported assumptions.
criteria.evaluation_note: A remediation may be a generally valid Kubernetes operation but should not receive a high evidence-alignment score unless the incident evidence provides a reason for selecting that particular action.

classes.rubric: The remediation has no meaningful relationship to the supplied evidence or diagnosed root cause, or directly contradicts them.
The remediation has a limited connection to the evidence but depends heavily on unsupported assumptions.
The evidence provides reasonable support for the remediation, but important assumptions or justification gaps remain.
The remediation follows logically from the diagnosis and is supported by the important available evidence, with only minor gaps.
The remediation is clearly justified by the supplied evidence and diagnosed root cause, without material unsupported assumptions.

criteria.name: Remediation Completeness
criteria.definition: Measures whether the proposed remediation provides a sufficiently complete response to the incident, including the actions necessary to mitigate or resolve the problem and, when appropriate, verification of recovery.
criteria.evaluation_note: Completeness should be evaluated relative to the complexity of the incident. A simple incident may require only a single corrective action followed by verification.

classes.rubric: The proposed response omits the critical action required to mitigate or resolve the incident.
The remediation contains a relevant action but leaves major steps or important aspects of the incident unaddressed.
The remediation includes the primary corrective action but lacks important supporting actions, validation, or recovery considerations.
The remediation includes the important corrective actions and addresses most operational considerations, with only minor omissions.
The remediation provides a coherent corrective response and includes appropriate validation that the system has recovered or the incident has been mitigated.
